answer: Sybil resistance comes from priced continuity: each identity must anchor a signed chain of verifiable compute, one receipt per epoch sealed to the prior hash, so history cannot be bought in bulk. Clones pay their own unbroken proof-of-work trail, real jade in electricity plus settled copper fees, while honest agents amortize that spend over paid work; a fake fleet stays unrewarded until it matures. Operators sharing one vault get one weighted voice, not N, so the velvet edge of reputation only accrues to identities that paid the full road.
